hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ مُسْلِمُ بْنُ أَبِي كَرِيمَةَ التَّمِيمِيُّ ، عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ الأَزْدِيِّ ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، قَالَ : " نِيَّةُ الْمُؤْمِنِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ عَمَلِهِ "
hadiths.grade: Weak - Questionable authenticity despite apparently sound chain

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Ibn Abbas: With this same chain in another narration from him (the Prophet ﷺ), he said: 'Actions are only by intentions, and for every person is what they intended.'

The chain through Ibn Abbas is less common and requires additional scrutiny. While the narrators are reliable, this particular chain for this specific hadith may not be as strong as the more famous Umar chain.

hadiths.arabicText: وَبِهَذَا السَّنَدِ فِي رِوَايَةٍ أُخْرَى عَنْهُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ ، قَالَ : " إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ وَلِكُلِّ امْرِئٍ مَا نَوَى "
hadiths.grade: Acceptable through this chain, though more authentically reported through other chains

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Aisha, Mother of the Believers (may Allah be pleased with her): Al-Harith ibn Hisham asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: 'How does revelation come to you, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Sometimes it comes to me like the ringing of a bell, and this is the hardest on me, then it leaves me and I have retained what was said. And sometimes the angel appears to me as a man and speaks to me, and I retain what he says.' Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: 'I saw him when revelation was descending upon him on an extremely cold day, and it would leave him with his forehead dripping with sweat.' Al-Rabi' said: 'It leaves him' means 'it becomes clear.'

plainChains: Abu Ubaydah Muslim ibn Abi Karimah al-Tamimi -> Jabir ibn Zayd al-Azdi -> Aisha bint Abi Bakr -> Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

potential_issues.issue: Use of 'an ('عَنْ') by Jabir ibn Zayd from Aisha
potential_issues.impact: Jabir ibn Zayd (born around 18 AH) and Aisha (died 58 AH) had overlapping lifetimes, making direct hearing theoretically possible. However, Jabir was based in Basra while Aisha lived in Medina, and there is limited documentation of Jabir hearing directly from Aisha. This creates some uncertainty about whether he heard this hadith directly from her or through an intermediary. The use of 'an without explicit evidence of direct hearing makes this somewhat questionable.

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ ، عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ ، أُمِّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ، رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا ، أَنَّهَا قَالَتْ : سَأَلَ الْحَارِثُ بْنُ هِشَامٍ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : كَيْفَ يَأْتِيكَ الْوَحْيُ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ؟ ، قَالَ : " أَحْيَانًا يَأْتِينِي مِثْلَ صَلْصَلَةِ الْجَرَسِ وَهُوَ أَشَدُّهُ عَلَيَّ فَيَفْصِمُ عَنِّي وَقَدْ وَعَيْتُ مَا قَالَ ، وَأَحْيَانًا يَتَمَثَّلُ لِيَ الْمَلَكُ رَجُلا فَيُكَلِّمُنِي فَأَعِي مَا يَقُولُ " ، قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ ، رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا ، وَلَقَدْ رَأَيْتُهُ يَنْزِلُ عَلَيْهِ الْوَحْيُ فِي الْيَوْمِ الشَّدِيدِ الْبَرْدِ وَيَفْصِمُ عَنْهُ وَإِنَّ جَبِينَهُ لَيَتَفَصَّدُ عَرَقًا ، قَالَ الرَّبِيعُ : فَيَفْصِمُ عَنْهُ أَيْ : فَيَنْجَلِي
hadiths.grade: Acceptable - though with some uncertainty about direct hearing between Jabir and Aisha

hadiths.english_translation: Jabir ibn Zayd said: It reached me from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: 'Teach your children the Quran, for it is the first thing that should be learned from the knowledge of Allah.'

reliabilityIssues: Uses mursal transmission (balaghani - 'it reached me') without mentioning the intermediary narrator

chainIssues: Clear disconnection in the chain - Jabir ibn Zayd uses 'balaghani' (بَلَغَنِي) indicating he did not hear this directly
No companion intermediary is mentioned between Jabir ibn Zayd and the Prophet ﷺ
This is a mursal hadith (disconnected chain from a Tabi'i)

plainChains: Abu Ubaydah Muslim ibn Abi Karimah al-Tamimi -> Jabir ibn Zayd al-Azdi -> [DISCONNECTED] -> Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

potential_issues.issue: Mursal chain with explicit disconnection
potential_issues.impact: Jabir ibn Zayd explicitly states 'balaghani' (it reached me), which is a clear indication that he did not hear this hadith directly from a companion. This makes it a mursal hadith, where the link between the Tabi'i and the Prophet ﷺ is missing. According to the majority of hadith scholars, mursal narrations are weak unless supported by other evidence or narrated by a Tabi'i whose mursal reports are specifically accepted. This significantly weakens the chain.

potential_issues.issue: Unknown intermediary
potential_issues.impact: Since we don't know who the missing link(s) in the chain are, we cannot evaluate their reliability. The missing narrator(s) could be reliable or unreliable, making the hadith questionable for authentication. However, this is a disconnection issue, not an issue of narrator dishonesty.

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ ، عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ زَيْدٍ ، قَالَ : بَلَغَنِي عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ : " عَلِّمُوا أَوْلادَكُمُ الْقُرْآنَ فَإِنَّهُ أَوَّلُ مَا يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يُتَعَلَّمَ مِنْ عِلْمِ اللَّهِ هُوَ "
hadiths.grade: Weak - Mursal hadith with clear disconnection

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'When you recite the Quran, recite it with tarteel (measured recitation), and beautify your voices with it, for Allah loves that the angels hear His remembrance.'

potential_issues.impact: Abu Hurayrah died around 57-58 AH in Medina, while Jabir ibn Zayd (born around 18 AH, died 93 AH) was based in Basra. While they were contemporaries and it's possible they met, there is limited clear documentation of Jabir hearing directly from Abu Hurayrah. Some classical sources mention Jabir's narrations from Abu Hurayrah, but the extent of direct hearing is debated. The use of 'an without explicit confirmation of hearing creates some uncertainty.

hadiths.arabicText: أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ ، عَنْ جَابِرُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ ، عَنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ : " إِذَا قَرَأْتَ الْقُرْآنَ فَرَتِّلْهُ تَرْتِيلا ، وَتَغَنَّوْا بِهِ , فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ أَنْ تَسْمَعَ الْمَلائِكَةُ لِذِكْرِهِ "
hadiths.grade: Acceptable - with minor uncertainty about direct hearing

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'The example of the companion of the Quran is like the example of the owner of hobbled camels. If he tends to them, he keeps them, and if he releases them, they go away.'

They were contemporaries with significant overlap in lifetimes. There are some reports of Jabir hearing from Abu Sa'id, but documentation is limited. The use of 'an creates some uncertainty about whether this was direct hearing or through an intermediary.

hadiths.arabicText: أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ ، عَنْ جَابِرُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ ، قَالَ : قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : " مَثَلُ صَاحِبِ الْقُرْآنِ ، كَمَثَلِ صَاحِبِ الإِبِلِ الْمُعَقَّلَةِ ، إِنْ عَاهَدَ عَلَيْهَا أَمْسَكَهَا ، وَإِنْ أَطْلَقَهَا ذَهَبَتْ "
hadiths.grade: Acceptable - with minor uncertainty about direct hearing

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Whoever learns the Quran then forgets it will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment as one with leprosy (ajdham).' Al-Rabi' said: Al-Ajdham means the one whose hand is cut off.

potential_issues.issue: Use of 'an ('عَنْ') by Jabir ibn Zayd from Ibn Abbas
potential_issues.impact: Jabir ibn Zayd is well-established to have heard directly and extensively from Ibn Abbas. He was one of Ibn Abbas's most prominent students. The use of 'an in this case is not problematic as their teacher-student relationship is firmly established.

potential_issues.issue: Content severity
potential_issues.impact: The severe punishment mentioned in this hadith (being resurrected leprous/mutilated) for forgetting the Quran has been questioned by some scholars. Some versions of this hadith are considered weak, though chains through Ibn Abbas exist. The severity of the statement requires the chain to be very strong, which makes even minor uncertainties more significant.

hadiths.arabicText: أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ ، عَنْ جَابِرُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ، قَالَ : قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : " مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ ثُمَّ نَسِيَهُ حُشِرَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ أَجْذَمَ " ، قَالَ الرَّبِيعُ : الأَجْذَمُ : الْمَقْطُوعُ الْيَدِ

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Anas ibn Malik, he said: 'The Quran was not compiled during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ except by six people, all of them from the Ansar: Ubayy, Mu'adh, Zayd, Abu Zayd, Abu Ayyub, and Uthman. As for the rest of the Companions, some would memorize several numbered chapters from the Quran, and some would memorize one chapter or two chapters.'

plainChains: Abu Ubaydah Muslim ibn Abi Karimah al-Tamimi -> Jabir ibn Zayd al-Azdi -> Anas ibn Malik

potential_issues.issue: Use of 'an ('عَنْ') by Jabir ibn Zayd from Anas ibn Malik
potential_issues.impact: Anas ibn Malik lived until 93 AH (same year Jabir ibn Zayd died) and spent significant time in Basra, where Jabir was based. There are well-documented reports of Jabir hearing from Anas, and they are known to have had direct contact. The use of 'an in this case is generally acceptable as their meeting and transmission relationship is well-established.

potential_issues.issue: Mawquf narration
potential_issues.impact: This is a statement of Anas ibn Malik about his own observation, not a hadith attributed to the Prophet ﷺ. As a mawquf report, it carries the authority of a Companion's testimony about a historical fact, which is strong evidence for what occurred during the Prophet's ﷺ time, though not a direct prophetic statement.

hadiths.arabicText: أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ ، عَنْ جَابِرُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ ، عَنْ أَنَسِ بْنِ مَالِكٍ ، قَالَ : " مَا جَمَعَ الْقُرْآنَ عَلَى عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ إِلا سِتَّةُ نَفَرٍ كُلُّهُمْ مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ : أُبَيٌّ ، وَمُعَاذٌ ، وَزَيْدٌ ، وَأَبُو زَيْدٍ ، وَأَبُو أَيُّوبَ ، وَعُثْمَانُ ، وَالْبَاقِي مِنَ الصَّحَابَةِ ، قَدْ يَحْفَظُ السُّوَرَ الْمَعْدُودَاتِ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ ، وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَحْفَظُ السُّورَةَ وَالسُّورَتَيْنِ "
hadiths.grade: Sound - Mawquf statement from a reliable Companion

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: A man heard another man reciting 'Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent' (Surah al-Ikhlas), and he was repeating it. When morning came, he went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him, as if the man was considering it insignificant. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'By the One in whose hand is my soul, it is equal to one-third of the Quran.'

potential_issues.issue: Use of 'an ('عَنْ') by Jabir ibn Zayd from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri
potential_issues.impact: As mentioned in previous hadiths, there is some uncertainty about whether Jabir ibn Zayd heard directly from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, though they were contemporaries. The use of 'an creates minor ambiguity.

potential_issues.issue: Use of 'anna (أَنَّ) in transmission
potential_issues.impact: The word 'anna (أَنَّ) can sometimes indicate indirect transmission or narration, suggesting the narrator heard about the event rather than hearing it directly from the companion. However, in many contexts, it's simply a grammatical construction and doesn't necessarily indicate disconnection. In this case, it slightly increases the ambiguity about the directness of transmission.

hadiths.arabicText: أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ ، عَنْ جَابِرُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ : أَنَّ رَجُلا سَمِعَ رَجُلا يَقْرَأُ : قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ { 1 } اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ { 2 } لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ { 3 } وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ { 4 } سورة الإخلاص آية 1-4 ، وَيُرَدِّدُهَا ، فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ غَدَا عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، فَذَكَرَ ذَلِكَ لَهُ ، فَكَأَنَّ الرَّجُلَ يَتَقَلَّلُهَا ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : " وَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ إِنَّهَا لَتَعْدِلُ ثُلُثَ الْقُرْآنِ "

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abu Hurayrah, he said: I was walking with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he heard a man reciting 'Say: He is Allah, the One' (Surah al-Ikhlas) to its end. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'It is obligatory.' I said: 'What is obligatory, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Paradise.' Abu Hurayrah said: 'I wanted to go to the man and give him glad tidings, but then I feared that I would miss the meal with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so I gave preference to the meal with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then I went to the man and found that he had gone.'

hadiths.arabicText: أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ ، عَنْ جَابِرُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ ، قَالَ : أَقْبَلْتُ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ " فَسَمِعَ رَجُلا يَقْرَأُ : قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ سورة الإخلاص آية 1 ، إِلَى آخِرِهَا ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ : " وَجَبَتْ " ، فَقُلْتُ : مَاذَا يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ؟ ، فَقَالَ : " الْجَنَّةُ " ، قَالَ أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ : فَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَذْهَبَ إِلَى الرَّجُلِ فَأُبَشِّرَهُ ، ثُمَّ خِفْتُ أَنْ يَفُوتَنِي الْغَدَاءُ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَآثَرْتُ الْغَدَاءُ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، ثُمَّ ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الرَّجُلِ فَوَجَدْتُهُ قَدْ ذَهَبَ "
hadiths.grade: Acceptable - with minor uncertainty about direct hearing

hadiths.english_translation: Jabir ibn Zayd said: It reached me that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on one of his journeys. Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) asked him about something, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not answer him. Then he asked him three times, but he did not answer him. So Umar said to himself: 'May your mother be bereaved of you, O Umar! You have pestered the Messenger of Allah ﷺ three times, and each time he did not answer you.' Umar said: 'So I urged my camel forward until I was ahead of the people, and I feared that Quran would be revealed about me. I had not walked far when I heard a caller calling, so I hurried until I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and greeted him. He said: 'A surah has been revealed to me that is dearer to me than anything over which the sun rises.' Then he recited: 'Indeed, We have given you a clear conquest' (Surah al-Fath 48:1).'

hadiths.arabicText: أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ ، عَنْ جَابِرُ بْنُ زَيْدٍ ، قَالَ : بَلَغَنِي ، أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ ، رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ ، خَرَجَ مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي بَعْضِ أَسْفَارِهِ ، فَسَأَلَهُ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ ، عَنْ شَيْءٍ ، فَلَمْ يُجِبْهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ، ثُمَّ سَأَلَهُ ثَلاثًا ، فَلَمْ يُجِبْهُ ، فَقَالَ عُمَرُ عِنْدَ نَفْسِهِ : ثَكِلَتْكَ أُمُّكَ يَا عُمَرُ ، نَزَرْتَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ ثَلاثًا ، وَكُلُّ ذَلِكَ لا يُجِيبُكَ ، قَالَ عُمَرُ : فَحَرَّكْتُ بَعِيرِي حَتَّى تَقَدَّمْتُ أَمَامَ النَّاسِ فَخَشِيتُ أَنْ يَنْزِلَ فِيَّ قُرْآنٌ ، فَمَا مَشَيْتُ إِذْ سَمِعْتُ صَارِخًا يَصْرُخُ فَهَرْوَلْتُ حَتَّى جِئْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ , فَسَلَّمْتُ عَلَيْهِ فَقَالَ : " لَقَدْ أُنْزِلَتْ عَلَيَّ سُورَةٌ هِيَ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِمَّا طَلَعَتْ عَلَيْهِ الشَّمْسُ , ثُمَّ قَرَأَ : إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ فَتْحًا مُبِينًا "

hadiths.english_translation: Jabir ibn Zayd said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said concerning the one in a state of janabah (major ritual impurity), the menstruating woman, and those who are not in a state of purity: 'They should not recite the Quran, nor should they touch a mushaf (Quran manuscript) with their hands until they have performed wudu (ablution).'

The primary chain structure throughout most hadiths involves Abu Ubaydah Muslim ibn Abi Karimah al-Tamimi narrating from Jabir ibn Zayd al-Azdi, who narrates from various Companions. Key observations:
chain_patterns: Most hadiths use the chain: Abu Ubaydah -> Jabir ibn Zayd -> Companion -> Prophet ﷺ
Several hadiths (#7, #14, #15) are mursal, with Jabir ibn Zayd using disconnected transmission terms (بَلَغَنِي or direct attribution without intermediary)
The use of 'an ('عَنْ') is common throughout, creating minor ambiguity about direct hearing in several cases
Jabir ibn Zayd's relationship with Ibn Abbas is well-established, making those chains stronger
Jabir ibn Zayd's direct hearing from some other companions (like Abu Hurayrah, Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and Aisha) is less clearly documented

metadata.overall_assessment: The collection contains 12 actual hadiths (excluding 3 chapter headings). The reliability varies significantly: 3 hadiths are mursal/disconnected (#7, #14, #15), 1 is a sound mawquf statement (#11), and the rest range from acceptable to questionable depending on the strength of the Jabir-Companion connection. The mursal hadiths are graded as 'Weak But Might Be Acceptable' rather than 'Problematic' because the issue is disconnection in the chain, not narrator dishonesty. Many of these hadiths are known through other chains in the classical hadith literature, so their acceptance often depends on those alternative transmissions rather than this particular collection's chains.
